name: details-canonical-target-set
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the `details` edge kind's ONE canonical rule is the `Note` target exclusion, enforced on both sides. The durable write surface (`rust.apg.layers.validate.validate_edge`) refuses a `Note`→`Note` `details` pair at write time, and the graph projection (`rust.apg.load.tables.spec_rel_pairs`) omits `Note` from its `Details` target list — so the excluded pair can neither be written nor silently dropped. `Note` stays reviewable: `Reviews` (`Feedback`→`Note`) is a distinct edge kind and is explicitly outside this law.

This law makes NO closed-set and NO no-loss claim. The write surface validates only the `Note` exclusion for `details`: code-ref drift validation in `rust.apg.layers.write.validate_change` is scoped to `kind == "implemented-by"` only, so a non-`Note` (code or dangling) `details` target is written unvalidated and a stale one is silent drift — not a violation of this law. The write surface's admitted set and the projection's target list are NOT asserted to be the same set: the projection's `Details` list additionally declares transient plan-store targets (`Plan`/`PlanPhase`/`Task`), written by the transient plan-JSONL path that never calls `validate_edge` and are not durable authored nodes.
